text:
sam_customer: Hey team — since yesterday we see sporadic 403s hitting POST /v1/generate from our prod service. ~1% of calls fail, no pattern yet. Sample request ids: req_7a3f, req_7b2c, req_7d00. Using python-sdk v1.4.2 in us-west-2. Can someone help with repro steps?

zoe_support: Thanks — can you share a minimal curl repro and the raw response body for one of the failing requests? Also confirm the exact Authorization header (redacted ok) and whether you see any retries upstream.

sam_customer: quick curl I used locally (works most times, sometimes returns 403):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ****REMOVED****" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-3-small","input":"hello"}'
```
Response when it fails: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"forbidden","message":"request not authorized","request_id":"req_7a3f"}

matt_eng: can you run the curl with verbose and include the x-request-id header (so we can match traces)? e.g. `-H "x-request-id: req_7a3f" -v`. Also capture the TLS handshake output if possible.

sam_customer: running now, attaching excerpt:
```
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (34.12.45.67) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> x-request-id: req_7a3f
> Authorization: Bearer ****
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< x-redwood-request-id: req_7a3f
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "request not authorized",
  "request_id": "req_7a3f"
}
```
No obvious retries in our logs, single attempt from lambda.

jenna_se: sharing quick minimal SDK repros you can paste into a container to reproduce locally. Keep auth token redacted.
Python:
```python
import requests
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer ****","Content-Type":"application/json","x-request-id":"req_7a3f"}
data = {"model":"llama-3-small","input":"hello"}
r = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", json=data, headers=headers, timeout=10)
print(r.status_code, r.text)
```
Node (fetch):
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ****', 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'x-request-id': 'req_7a3f' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'llama-3-small', input: 'hello' })
}).then(r => r.text().then(t => console.log(r.status, t)));
```
Go (curl-style):
```go
package main
import ("net/http"; "strings"; "io/ioutil"; "fmt")
func main(){
  client := &http.Client{}
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST","https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", strings.NewReader(`{"model":"llama-3-small","input":"hello"}`))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer ****")
  req.Header.Set("x-request-id","req_7a3f")
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type","application/json")
  resp, _ := client.Do(req)
  b,_ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode, string(b))
}
```

zoe_support: perfect — can you also run our debug collector from the instance (if you can) to capture local env + network traces: `redwood-debug collect --request-id req_7a3f --out /tmp/redwood_dbg_req_7a3f.tar.gz` and upload to the support dropbox link? If you can't run it, the curl verbose + app logs are enough.

sam_customer: running collector now, ETA ~30s, will upload to the link you DM'd. One more data point: failure ratio spikes after bursts of ~200rps then drops. Could be a throttling/edge rule?

matt_eng: noted — we'll correlate with edge logs once we have the bundle. If you can, include a short HAR or tcpdump of a failing attempt. I'll grep for req_7a3f in the infra traces when the bundle is up.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: just an FYI — there was a config push 2 hours ago to edge-auth (rev c3f9) but no rollbacks since.

zoe_support: thanks — once bundle is uploaded I'll escalate to infra with the request ids and the code snippets so they can run the same in a sandbox. If it looks like auth edge mis-eval we'll route to security for token validation logic.

sam_customer: bundle uploaded to the DM link, file name redwood_dbg_req_7a3f.tar.gz. Thanks, please keep me posted.

matt_eng: got it — pinging infra and adding req_7a3f, req_7b2c, req_7d00 to the ticket. Expect an update in ~45–90m. :thumbsup:
